extracted.intended_audience: Prospective and current peer reviewers for the American Economic Review (AER)
extracted.subtask_short: AER peer review for journal submissions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for conducting peer review of manuscripts submitted to the American Economic Review, including procedural requirements (submission system, anonymity) and substantive evaluation criteria (empirical robustness, identification, contribution, theory quality, and overall publication-worthiness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity (single-blind review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts submitted to the American Economic Review are reviewed in a single-blind fashion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must exclude their names from report text and filenames to maintain anonymity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest handling
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal collects disclosure statements from all coauthors, but evaluation should focus on scientific merit rather than conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing a submission, emphasize whether 'the conclusions in the paper are robust, credible, and worthy of publication' rather than allowing disclosed conflicts to drive the evaluation. (The journal collects disclosures separately.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission and review system procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews are managed through ScholarOne Manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers access submission instructions and manage reviews via their Reviewer Center after logging in to ScholarOne.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended external referee resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The AER recommends external guidance that may be helpful to referees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested resources include a brief referee guidelines document from Econometrica and a more comprehensive guidance piece in the Journal of Economic Perspectives by Berk, Harvey, and Hirshleifer. Reviewers may consult these for additional best practices and evaluation perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness of empirical results
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the robustness of empirical results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether empirical findings hold under reasonable alternative specifications, checks, and sensitivity analyses; robustness is a central component of the AER referee model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credibility of identification strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Credibility of the paper's identification strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the empirical design convincingly identifies causal effects (where claimed), including the plausibility of assumptions and the strength of the identification approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive contribution to the literature
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the importance and novelty of the paper's contribution relative to existing work and whether it advances understanding in a way suitable for a leading general-interest economics journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of theoretical analysis (where relevant)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of theoretical analysis where relevant to the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the rigor, clarity, and relevance of any theoretical framework or modeling, including whether theory supports empirical work or provides important new insights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worthiness of publication in a top general-interest economics journal
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the paper is worthy of publication in a top general-interest economics journal (AER).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the combination of robustness, identification credibility, substantive contribution, and theoretical quality to judge whether the manuscript meets the high bar for AER publication.
